proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 80, 9^n is congruent to 9^(n mod 11) modulo 23.

argument.text: At n = 0 both sides equal 1 modulo 23.
The residue 9 has order 11 modulo 23: for every n in [0, 69], 9^(n+11) is congruent to 9^n modulo 23.
Every integer n in [1, 80] is even or odd, so the two cases below are exhaustive.
Every n in [0, 80] falls in exactly one residue class modulo 11.
There exists an integer n in [1, 80] with n^2 > 80.
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 80].
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 80 we have n^2 >= 2n.
The previous estimate holds on [2, 80] and the boundary value n = 1 was handled separately above, so by transitivity the estimate holds on the whole of [1, 80].
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 80: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
Periodicity plus the base case gives the statement for every n in [0, 80].
